approval_required_for: Architecture or design_space changes, including changes to operator decomposition, layer topology, pipeline boundaries, or major scheduling assumptions.
Pipeline or memory-layout changes, including address map, transfer unit, DDR/AXI ordering, stream order, runtime ABI, or host-buffer layout changes.

Numeric policy changes, including precision, quantization, accumulation policy, comparison tolerance, or replacement of golden-reference policy; direct golden-output edits or tolerance loosening to force pass remain forbidden.
Major template-library changes or free-form RTL/code-template rewrites outside approved bounded repair scopes.
Backend/app-shell target selection when board materials or Vivado evidence are ambiguous or conflicting.
LLM model override, consumption of fallback diagnostics as successful decisions, or bypass of enforced LLM review.
Backtrack beyond current-stage input repair scope or promotion of artifacts across an unresolved retry/backtrack/trust barrier.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block SACG extraction and downstream implementation decisions; create a bounded current-stage retry or backtrack request with a trust barrier; do not waive checkers, edit golden outputs, loosen tolerances, or claim pass from absent evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: Convert the summarized case_adapter acceptance/evidence_gates, human_agent_boundary, tool_protocols, prepared_inputs errors, and relevant SACG memory state into checker-backed audit artifacts. The supplied summary shows presence but not pass evidence, so no SACG extraction or downstream implementation decision should proceed until these checks produce evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep candidate artifacts quarantined from SACG extraction; require approval for architecture, numeric, memory-layout, pipeline, or major-template changes; otherwise repair only within the bounded input-preparation contract and rerun the boundary/protocol checker pack.
executable_actions.rationale: If the boundary audit finds missing checker coverage, conflicting approval/forbidden rules, non-empty hidden errors, or unsupported evidence gates, create bounded retry/backtrack artifacts. No open memory blocker is visible now, but any new same-stage blocker must be recorded before downstream consumption.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify the inconsistency as a current-stage blocker when it affects input acceptance/evidence gates, human boundary, or tool protocol; otherwise emit an explicit later-stage action with approvals. Do not start SACG extraction until the readiness decision is checker-backed.
executable_actions.rationale: After boundary audit artifacts exist, verify that task, model, shape, numeric, data-order, template, memory, runtime, implementation, and board facts are consistently represented before SACG extraction.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block promotion; regenerate the agent decision with the locked model or an approved override path, then rerun the boundary/protocol audit.
executable_actions.rationale: LLM policy is enforce=true, so boundary decisions and protocol interpretation must be real agent outputs and must not be replaced by fallback diagnostics, static keyword matching, or unreviewed scripts.

executable_actions.on_failure: Record a later-stage backend recovery blocker and require bounded approval for ambiguous shell targets; do not allow runtime bitstream or board-runtime actions to rely on guessed target names.
executable_actions.rationale: Ensure the tool_protocols and human boundary require backend/app-shell target discovery to cite supplied board materials and real Vivado evidence, with bounded approval when evidence is ambiguous, instead of guessing integration target names.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep audit artifacts local and block cross-stage handoff until SACG memory either records the blockers or explicitly records that no retry/backtrack/barrier state is open.
executable_actions.rationale: Preserve the audit outcome, explicit absence or presence of retry/backtrack requests, and any contamination barriers in shared SACG memory before handoff.

LLM policy is enforce=true with locked_model gpt-5.5; fallback diagnostic records must not be consumed as successful agent decisions.

Tool protocols for later verification/backend work should encode the three-layer repair loop: leaf/operator modules first, then connected single-transformer-layer kernel, then board-accurate AXI/DDR wrapped system. A failed layer must route through tool-output evidence, CCTG/contract-guided localization, bounded repair, and rerun before promotion.

Verifier capability gaps must be classified as checker or golden-reference repair needs, not as hardware correctness evidence. Real RTL/tool liveness, value, order, or protocol failures must be localized to the earliest causal boundary/module before code repair is proposed.
proposed_actions: Run the boundary/protocol checker pack over case_adapter, human_agent_boundary, tool_protocols, prepared_inputs, and the human/tool constraints; produce the required audit report, coverage matrix, approval/forbidden list, and repair-boundary gap list.
If checker gaps appear, generate a current-stage retry/backtrack request and artifact trust barrier, explicitly distinguishing repairable current-stage gaps from later-stage tool actions.
After boundary/protocol checks pass, run a cross-layer evidence gate over task, model, shape, numeric, template, board, memory, runtime, and tool facts before SACG extraction.
Run LLM/protocol quality checks to ensure decisions are real enforced-LLM agent outputs and not fallback diagnostics or static keyword matches.
Audit backend/app-shell target-discovery policy statically so later board integration is evidence-cited and ambiguity routes to approval rather than guessed names.
Update sacg_memory with the boundary audit outcome and any new retry, backtrack, or contamination-barrier state before handoff.
risks: Checker coverage risk: visible summaries do not prove that case_adapter acceptance/evidence_gates cover model, shape, numeric policy, data order, memory/runtime, implementation, and board facts.

Human-boundary risk: without detailed approval_required/auto_allowed/forbidden contents, an automated flow could accidentally permit forbidden actions such as checker bypass, tolerance loosening, golden-output modification, free-form RTL rewrite, or unsupported hardware-pass claims.
Tool-protocol risk: without expanded protocol details, downstream stages may rely on static scripts or human memory instead of bounded tool evidence and acceptance checkers.
Prepared-input risk: prepared_inputs.errors=[] may mask non-empty case_adapter.errors or insufficient evidence-gate coverage because those details were not visible in the supplied summary.

Repair-boundary risk: bounded repair/backtrack rules are not proven. Any failed boundary/protocol checker must create a current-stage retry/backtrack request and artifact trust barrier rather than allowing downstream consumption.

Cross-layer consistency risk: model decoder assumptions, tensor shapes, numeric precision/tolerance, data order, memory layout, runtime ABI, template bindings, and board deployment facts could diverge if SACG extraction starts before the boundary audit passes.

Backend/app-shell risk: target discovery must cite supplied board materials and real Vivado evidence. If evidence is ambiguous, the system must request bounded approval instead of guessing target names.
LLM-governance risk: because LLM planning is mandatory, any fallback or non-LLM diagnostic artifact must be quarantined from successful agent decision paths.

The candidate shows prepared_inputs.errors is empty and required boundary-related artifact classes are present, but checker execution evidence and detailed coverage for case_adapter acceptance/evidence_gates, human_agent_boundary, tool_protocols, and bounded repair/backtrack rules are not visible. Run the bounded checker pack and record any retry/backtrack/trust-barrier state before promotion.
